skill.name: stripe-automation
skill.description: Automate Stripe customer, payment, subscription, invoice, product, price, and refund workflows through Rube MCP.
skill.summary: Guides Stripe operations through Rube MCP with tool sequences, required parameters, and common billing pitfalls.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external command findings are false positives from Markdown backticks around tool names and parameters. The hardcoded Rube MCP URL is a real external dependency, and semantic review found risk from privileged Stripe operations without explicit approval or trust-boundary guidance. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: High-impact Stripe mutations do not require explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Before payments, captures, subscriptions, invoices, or refunds, show amount, currency, customer, object ID, and operation type, then require user approval.

remediation.issue: Third-party MCP trust boundary is not documented.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that Rube MCP mediates Stripe authorization, list expected permissions, and advise users to review access and revoke it when no longer needed.

remediation.issue: Financial workflows lack idempotency and test-mode guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend test mode for validation and idempotency keys for payment creation, refunds, and invoice or subscription mutations where supported.

remediation.issue: The setup says no API keys are needed without explaining authorization impact.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that OAuth or delegated authorization can still grant sensitive Stripe account access through the MCP provider.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Stripe connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `stripe`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- `amount`: Amount in smallest currency unit (e.g., cents for USD)
- `items`: Array of price items (price_id and quantity)
- Invoices auto-finalize by default; use `auto_advance: false` for draft invoices
- `amount`: Partial refund amount (omit for full refund)
- Pass `starting_after` with last object ID for next page
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Stripe allows duplicate customers with the same email; search first to avoid duplicates
- `items`: Array of price items (price_id and quantity)
- Subscriptions require a valid customer with a payment method

semantic_findings.title: High-Impact Stripe Actions Lack Explicit Approval Step
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md lists workflows for creating or confirming payments, capturing charges, creating subscriptions and invoices, and issuing refunds. It does not require an explicit user approval step before these financial mutations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented tool sequences include direct money movement and billing state changes. The surrounding workflow text does not show a confirmation gate, amount preview, or test-mode requirement.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party MCP Handles Stripe Authorization
semantic_findings.description: The setup directs users to add an external Rube MCP endpoint and connect the Stripe toolkit through RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS. This creates a trust boundary for Stripe account access that is not explained in the skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint and Stripe connection instructions are explicit in the setup section. The risk depends on user authorization scope, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.user_title: Automate Stripe Operations with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Stripe operations require exact IDs, amount units, and tool sequences. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows for common Stripe tasks.
actual_capabilities: Search, list, create, and update Stripe customers through Rube MCP.
Create payment intents, confirm payment intents, list charges, and capture charges.
Create, retrieve, list, and update Stripe subscriptions.
Create, list, and search invoices with collection method and due date guidance.
List and search products, prices, refunds, and related IDs.
Explain Stripe amount units, pagination, object ID prefixes, and common pitfalls.
limitations: Requires a connected Rube MCP server and active Stripe authorization.
Does not include built-in approval gates for charges, refunds, or subscription changes.
Depends on current Rube tool schemas and Stripe account permissions.
Does not process Stripe webhooks or build custom checkout interfaces.

use_cases.title: Customer Support Updates
use_cases.description: Search customers, review billing records, and update customer metadata after verifying the customer ID.

use_cases.title: Revenue Operations Review
use_cases.description: List subscriptions, invoices, products, and prices to reconcile account state before billing changes.

use_cases.title: Developer Billing Tasks
use_cases.description: Create test payment intents, subscriptions, invoices, or refunds while checking amount units and object IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Customer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Stripe automation skill to search for a customer by email. Show the matching customer IDs before suggesting any update.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Draft Invoice
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Rube MCP to create a draft Stripe invoice for this customer. Confirm collection method, due date, and auto_advance setting first.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Subscription Change
prompt_templates.prompt: List the customer subscriptions, retrieve the target subscription, and summarize the price IDs before preparing an update.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refund Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the charge, confirm the refund amount in smallest currency units, and prepare the refund request only after my approval.

output_examples.input: Find a customer by email and update the billing note.
output_examples.output: The skill first searches customers, shows matching customer IDs, asks which customer to update, then prepares the metadata change.

output_examples.input: Refund 50 dollars on a specific charge.
output_examples.output: The skill converts the amount to 5000 cents, verifies the charge, and asks for approval before creating a partial refund.

output_examples.input: Create a subscription for a customer with a known price.
output_examples.output: The skill retrieves available subscription tools, confirms the customer and price item, then prepares the subscription request.

best_practices: Search or retrieve objects before creating charges, subscriptions, invoices, or refunds.
Confirm amounts in the smallest currency unit before every payment or refund action.
Use test mode or limited permissions when validating new Stripe workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not create direct charges when a payment intent flow is available.
Do not issue refunds or capture payments without explicit user approval.
Do not assume email addresses uniquely identify Stripe customers.

faq.question: Does this skill require Rube MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires Rube MCP and an active Stripe connection through the stripe toolkit.

faq.question: Can it charge customers?
faq.answer: It documents payment intent, charge, and capture workflows. Users should require explicit approval before any money movement.

faq.question: Does it store Stripe API keys?
faq.answer: No evidence in SKILL.md shows stored API keys. It instructs users to connect through Rube MCP authorization.

faq.question: Can it manage subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists subscription create, retrieve, list, and update workflows through Stripe tools.

faq.question: What Stripe objects can it handle?
faq.answer: It covers customers, charges, payment intents, subscriptions, invoices, products, prices, refunds, and payment methods.

faq.question: What is the main safety concern?
faq.answer: The main concern is high-impact financial actions through a third-party MCP without explicit approval gates.
